title: The Unity of Essence and the Cooperation of the Trinity
english: He is inseparable from the divinity because he cooperates with and provides all things to all alongside the self-sufficient and almighty God the Father, not deferring [it] until tomorrow, since the Spirit of the Father is also co-knowing and co-knowing, possessing an uncreated being and reigning with Him, having inherited the divinity from where He proceeded as a co-inherent. Furthermore, the all-seeing and almighty Christ, together with the power of His most venerable Spirit, performed signs and wonders and cast out demons, as the hierophants explained: Michael says, 'Thus says the Lord against the prophets who mislead my people' (Micah 7:6), and shortly after brings: 'For there shall be no one who hears them, unless I fill strength in the spirit of the Lord and of judgment and of power.' Thus, he says to perform strength in the spirit of the Lord, in order to also reveal the Trinity and the bond of its nature. He alludes to judgment, in which there is no longer room for repentance or for the one who hears; 'for,' he says, 'in that abyss, who will confess to you?' And 'I will fill strength' stands for 'I will make a great retribution with the divine Spirit.' And Paul, the most tested of apostles, to the Ephesians says: 'For this reason I bow my knees to God the Father, from whom every family is named in heaven and on earth, that He may give to you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with power through His Spirit, so that Christ may dwell in the inner man' (Ephesians 3:14-17); and to the Romans: 'I have therefore confidence in Christ Jesus toward God. For I do not dare to speak anything of which Christ did not accomplish through me, by word and deed, for the obedience of the Gentiles, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Holy Spirit' (Romans 15:18). Hypostases of similar nature are worthy of similar honor; therefore, this saying is close to: 'Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God' (1 Cor 1:24). Matthew says from the Savior: 'But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you' (Matthew 12:28). And as He acts in the illumination: it is impossible, then, to exist as one through harmony and energy without there being a single essence; and for this reason the Lord says at times: 'The Father who remains in me, He Himself does the works' (John 14:10); and at other times, as has now been said: 'I cast out by the Spirit of God...'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Economy of the Mystery and Angelic Limitation
english: A righteous man and one fearing God, being testified to by all the nations of the Jews, was informed by a holy angel that he was to be brought into his house and to hear words from you. You indeed, if you had remained silent and had shut the mouths of slanders, would have acted much more effectively.

But we, returning toward the most perfect goal and providing this summary and cheerfulness to those about to receive [us], and instilling more of the orthodox zeal, say that just as no communion of nature exists in creation toward the uncreated nature, so also no such [communion] exists in [mere] information. For the one announces, and the other, not knowing, might be enabled to speak by the Holy Spirit, and from this he receives the name 'angel'; but the Holy Spirit, since He knows all things of God, as Paul confirms, informs divinely, just as the Father, seeing with the sleepless eyes of the deity what is willed, [informs] the Father and the Son, and not in a servile way, like a bodyguard angel. For 'the slave does not know what his master is doing' (Luke 12:47), nor can the one of the same substance [possess] the knowledge of the other being of a different substance; for to each nature, the knowledge not belonging to it and memory are co-participating in error; but even what is known by the generated nature is lost by time. Therefore, even here, the ignorant ones, rushing into the field of the battle of the Word, have gone astray.

For it is written: 'And while Peter was remembering the word, the Holy Spirit said to him: Behold, three men are seeking you. But arising, go with them, distinguishing nothing; because I have sent them.' (Acts 10:19-20). Having come down to the men, Peter said: 'Behold, I am the one you are seeking; what is the reason for which you have come?' (Acts 10:21). And they said: 'Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man' (Acts 10:24), and the following, as it is intended. So, even before good judges, the angel's informing appears to be learned from the Holy Spirit. For to foretell with certainty is a distinguished mark of deity; and this is for the good of those hearing, so that, being made secure, they might be saved. Furthermore, do you not think that by proposing such things, one is somewhat flattering the creation, or perhaps criticizing him who has adorned his own works with the words spoken about him through abundance?
And of his grace. For from this he did not insult himself at all, but rather he showed himself to be praiseworthy, and his works were habitually made bright.

We, indeed, if we carry the matter of the Holy Spirit's endowment as something of divine dignity, and it suffices by itself for testimony, yet we brought forth not only that, but also a multitude of other high and indisputable proofs; if you attend to these without contradiction, you will certainly be less speechless than the fish. Therefore Paul most clearly exposes your trickery, having written to the Ephesians: 'To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given in the Gentiles, to preach the unsearchable riches of Christ and to enlighten all, what is the economy of the mystery having been hidden from the ages in God the Creator, so that now might be known to the rulers and authorities in the heavenly places through the church the manifold wisdom of God' (Eph 3:8). Understand, therefore, how much the nature of the angels is lacking in knowing of itself things that are to come and in endowment; for even through this church of God in this world, which we are, they learn the great things. And toward persuasion, one can grasp something regarding this, which he wrote to the Colossians thus: 'This mystery which was hidden before the ages and from the generations, which has now been revealed to his saints' (Col 1:26). For before this, he says, it was known to God alone.

Toward these things, and also that which concerns the benefit of all men, of which I speak concerning the unchosen economy, this is raised by Peter to the rhetoricians, as it was foretold: 'Angels desire to look into things' (1 Pet 1:12), he says. And if they had any innate knowledge, they would not long to even stoop into it, but because they do not have it, they fall into a sort of excessive desire, like men, for those things whose knowledge is not above them. For it has become nature to overlook easily found things and to make the rarer things a matter of effort. And yet even this is not according to their nature, for by the common reason of their nature I do not say that all are obligated to some extent. title: The Archangels and the Incarnation
english: Are they about to exercise authority in administering, as God is able to have? If these do not even administer from themselves or by their own power, the matter itself is a self-evident proof of a certain division. Because you commanded to act rashly and without investigation regarding the rebuke and the accusation, merely according to the word in common, and not regarding the matter itself.

For if others should happen to say that God the Father administers and is good, it is not proper for us to say the opposite. Let me say something else to you: 'Look lest one says that the one who administered to the centurion, the Holy of Holies, the Savior, spoke [of the centurion]; for by using this name, the Scripture appears to be hidden with much expression and divinity regarding him, in order to announce in the economy as a Son the Father's will. For he did not say by name, as he is wont to say: Michael, Gabriel, or such-and-such.'

What, then, could anyone reasonably blame among all our words? And what should they rebuke in one who possesses nothing but the duty to be straight in the orthodox faith? And how could it not be worthy of belief, that the Holy Spirit administers royally or divinely, while the angels administer liturgically or diaconically? How difficult, then, it is, as it is said, to be a 'shouter.'

Just as for one who is not above governing, so it is difficult to teach; for to one in whom the grace of the Divine Spirit, working salvation together with the Father and the Son with men, is not present, nor is there found the safety of knowing, and the response given from the knowledge of faithful men, even within the riddles of the oracles, and to whom there is no flow of speech without contentious, dialectical, and various preconception.

But I know clearly, O well-pleasing ones and angels of God dwelling in the heavenly light, that you yourselves, as blameless and perfect, were not offended by the things said by me, on account of the angels who are like you according to nature, not according to the praise of opinion; those by whom from the beginning rebuke followed, as also those who seem to you most unbelieving toward the struggle for the truth. For the word is mine concerning the Divine Spirit, who enlightens all things and is zealous for the divine things for the creatures of the Father and His only-begotten [Son]...

You are family, having sanctified both yourselves and being glory-shared by you together with the Father and the Son through the Trisagion hymn. Rather, you also partook of this Spirit of the one and only hypostasis of God, having not spoken aloud of Him to me. And you perhaps wished to celebrate in this part of the book, through an excess of your goodwill, that the words spoken by many and now by me concerning the Septenary and the consubstantial Trinity should not ever be subject to silence, and that all men should spend the time from the facts toward such a hypothesis.

Therefore, because of this, by the judgment of the Most High: you, O holy Michael, were chosen to rule the 76 incorporeal hosts and were honored as if by a belt, and you exist as a certain fragrance of the all-ruling, all-pure, and compassionate Trinity; and you, O holy Gabriel, were chosen to minister to the mystery of the ineffable economy, as a faithful and constant one. One is honored by another with a God-given gift, such as not even others have, and such as not even we have; but even we have such as not even you have.

For the God Word became man, not through sinful angels, but through men in sin, unchangeably, unmixedly, without sin, ineffably, as He knew and willed, from the Virgin and according to her flesh, and became all of us, remaining what He was and is and will be, one and the same. 'For one,' He says, 'is the holy one, one is the Lord Jesus Christ unto the glory of God the Father' (1 Cor 8:6). And thus, as He ascended from earth to the heavens, the second [coming] shall come, with myriads of myriads of blessed angelic phalanxes ministering to Him, and He will yet judge and act according to His philanthropy.

Therefore, after the churches and houses, the pleasant places named after your appellation, O pleasing company of archangels, were established not only in cities, but also in narrow places, privately, in houses and in fields, adorned with gold and silver or even ivory; and men, even to the more remote places where they are lodged, having the pleasant places thrust forward as if they had attained a magistracy, do not hesitate to take a sea, or if necessary, a long road of many sufficient days.
